_comment: Nothing here is needed to use the skills. install/user/settings.json is the file that
matters, and it holds the permission rules and nothing else; this one is one person's
preferences. Take what you want and ignore the rest.
It carries no permissions key on purpose, and scripts/validate.sh asserts that. The
permission template's claim to cover this toolkit and nothing else has to stay
checkable, which it would not be if opinion could accumulate in a second file that
attribution empties the trailers Claude Code would otherwise append to a commit message
and a PR body. install/user/CLAUDE.md asks for that in prose, which an agent can
forget; this is the setting that enforces it.
Two of these cost money on the account that adopts them, and are here because they are
what the review skills are actually used with rather than because they are safe
defaults. effortLevel raises the reasoning budget on every turn. skipWorkflowUsageWarning
removes the prompt that warns a multi-agent workflow is about to spend a lot -- see
'What an adversarial review costs' in the README for what that is, and leave this one
out until you have paid for a few runs knowingly.
